text.tspan: Abstract.
Pipelines that use large language models as pairwise judges remove
position bias and length bias in separate steps, assuming the two add. I show that
this assumption matters, can be tested without human labels, and is easy to test
wrongly. On the win-rate scale, any correction that applies one position offset across
length conditions misstates the verbose-versus-terse contrast by exactly half the
position×length interaction; swap-averaging and stratified correction are exact. The
Swap-Symmetry Interaction Test estimates that interaction from the four swap cells
of each stimulus as a difference of means. Two artefacts can manufacture what it
measures: coding a tie as a vote for slot B, which breaks swap symmetry, and link
curvature near the ceiling. Corrected for both, seven judges from six families show
no individually significant interaction, but a pooled one survives: +4.7 win-rate
points, with position bias absent at matched length and present only when the target
is longer.
Proposition 1. Exact because it concerns cell
means only; the log-odds version fails by
non-collapsibility.
The tie artefact appeared in this project's
own first analysis and is corrected here.
95% CI [1.6, 7.8]; sign-flip p = 0.012 over 12
distinct stimuli.
